title: ～かける — half-done, in the middle of ～
summary: Shows an action that is half-done or just begun and not finished. It attaches to a verb stem, and ～かけの＋noun is a common form.

patterns.form: Vます形（ます抜き）＋かける
Vます形（ます抜き）＋かけの＋N

body.p: 読みかける means having started to read but not finished. The noun-modifying form is very common: 読みかけの本, 飲みかけのコーヒー, 食べかけのパン. It also covers stopping partway, as in 言いかけて、やめた.
～始める is about the beginning of an action, while ～かける stresses the unfinished middle. ～終わる means finished; ～かけ means unfinished.

examples.ja: 飲（の）みかけのコーヒーが置（お）いてある。
examples.romaji: Nomikake no kōhī ga oite aru.
examples.tr: There's a half-finished coffee left here.

examples.ja: 言（い）いかけてやめられると、かえって気（き）になる。
examples.romaji: Iikakete yamerareru to, kaette ki ni naru.
examples.tr: When someone starts to say something and then stops, it bothers me even more.

examples.ja: 読（よ）みかけの本（ほん）が机（つくえ）に置（お）いたままだ。
examples.romaji: Yomikake no hon ga tsukue ni oita mama da.
examples.tr: A half-read book is left on the desk.

pitfalls: かける marks a halfway state, not a deliberate start. 勉強をかける is not a phrase.
Before a noun use ～かけの: 飲みかけのコーヒー, not 飲みかけコーヒー.
